newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India offers May high aromatic naphtha from Madras.
newsitem.headline: India offers May high aromatic naphtha from Madras.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued a tender to sell 27,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) lifting May 17-19 from Madras on the east coast, industry sources said on Thursday.
The tender closes May 8 and is valid for a day.

IOC's last HAN tender from Madras, for 28,000 tonnes lifting April 25-27, was awarded at a $31.00 per tonne discount to Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, a much lower price than its previous award for an earlier cargo lifting March 27-29 at a $22.28 discount.
Traders said weak gasoline prices have pressured down the price for naphtha grade used in the production of gasoline.
